intro: The third table completes the system, and it is the one with the clearest logic: when there is no article at all, the adjective takes over the article's job entirely and wears the der/die/das ending itself. Nominative: starker Kaffee (der → -er), frische Milch (die → -e), frisches Brot (das → -es), nette Leute (die → -e). Accusative: starken Kaffee (den → -en), the rest unchanged. Dative: starkem Kaffee (dem → -em), frischer Milch (der → -er), kaltem Wasser (dem → -em), netten Leuten (den → -en, and the noun takes -n). Genitive m/n is the one exception — guten Weines, not gutes, because the noun's -s already marks the case. The Nullartikel appears with mass nouns (Kaffee, Milch, Wetter), plurals (Leute, Kinder), after numbers (zwei kleine Kinder) and in headlines and ads — so flat ads, menus and newspapers are full of it.
tips[0].title: No article → the adjective wears the article's ending
tips[0].text: der → -er (starker Kaffee), die → -e (frische Milch), das → -es (frisches Brot), die Pl → -e (nette Leute), den → -en, dem → -em, der (Dat f) → -er, den (Dat Pl) → -en.
tips[0].trap: English 'strong coffee' has nothing to show; German has to show the case somewhere, and with no article, the adjective is the only place.
tips[0].check.why: mit takes the dative, and with no article the adjective wears the dative feminine ending of der: frischer Butter.
tips[1].title: Where the Nullartikel lives
tips[1].text: Mass nouns (Kaffee, Wasser, Musik, Wetter), plurals without an article (Kinder, Leute, Freunde), after numbers (drei kleine Kinder), after viele / einige / wenige (viele nette Leute), in ads and headlines (Schöne Wohnung, ruhige Lage).
tips[1].check.why: A number is not an article, so the adjective takes the plural die-ending itself: drei kleine Katzen.
tips[2].title: Dative plural: -en on the adjective AND -n on the noun
tips[2].text: mit netten Leuten, mit kleinen Kindern, bei guten Freunden. Two markers, both required.
tips[2].check.why: Dative plural needs two markers: -en on the adjective and -n on the noun.
tips[3].title: Take the article, cut the d-, glue the rest
tips[3].text: der Kaffee → (d)er → starkER Kaffee. dem Kaffee → (d)em → starkEM Kaffee. die Milch → (d)ie → frischE Milch. It works for every slot except genitive m/n.
tips[3].check.why: das Bier → cut the d- → -as becomes -es: kaltes Bier, the neuter nominative ending.
tips[3].visual.caption: With no article, the adjective borrows the article's ending. Only the masculine and neuter genitive take -en.

tips[3].visual.rows[1].label: Akk
tips[3].visual.rows[2].label: Dat
remember[0]: No article: adjective = article ending (starker, frische, frisches, nette).
table.caption: Adjective with no article
mistakes[0].why: Before a noun the adjective always has an ending; here it shows the accusative.
mistakes[3].why: Genitive masculine/neuter with no article: the noun already ends in -s, so the adjective takes -en.
hook: Menus, flat ads and headlines drop the article — so the adjective has to carry the ending all by itself.
recall.known: From the two adjective-ending lessons: after der and after ein.
recall.today: With no article at all, the adjective takes the article's own ending.
